notes: I opened the filing index and all three documents, and found no Illumina supply terms. The filing is Freenome's DRS/A (accession 0001140361-26-011956, filed 2026-03-30), tied to its business combination. EX-10.16 is a Roche Sequencing Solutions License and Option Agreement dated 17 Nov 2025. It gives Roche an option on an exclusive ex-US license to Freenome's cancer-detection kits and a preferred-partner right for ex-US central testing. The parties also agreed to evaluate running Freenome assays on Roche's SBX platform, and Roche pays a $75M option fee through a convertible note. The agreement has no flow-cell pricing, discounts, minimum purchases or most-favored pricing, and option-exercise fees and royalty rates are redacted. EX-10.25 is a New England Biolabs reagent supply agreement (Feb 2022, Amendment 1 Nov 2022) with minimum annual purchases and redacted prices. It is not an Illumina contract and covers EM-seq reagents, not sequencing consumables. I read about 0-100K and 200-300K characters of the 327K-character main document. It had one passing Roche reference (Roche ~18.11% of New Freenome) and no Illumina, NovaSeq or sequencer-supply terms. I did not read characters 100K-200K, the Freenome business section, or the last ~27K. Freenome's Illumina supply terms may sit there, but no Illumina exhibit was filed. The only link to the thesis is a weak 2B datapoint: a diagnostics company that is also a Roche equity holder and licensee has agreed to evaluate its assays on SBX/Axelios. The details are unquantified, so I did not log an item.
